GNU grep 3.11 with PCRE2 10.42: grep-perl ("grep -P")
Licences: GNU grep – GPL-3.0-or-later (COPYING in this folder); PCRE2 – BSD 3-clause with the PCRE2
exemption (PCRE2-LICENCE in this folder).
Upstream sources: https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/grep/grep-3.11.tar.xz
                  https://github.com/PCRE2Project/pcre2/releases/download/pcre2-10.42/pcre2-10.42.tar.bz2

This program was compiled to WebAssembly for the practical "AI agents for bioinformatics", whose
terminal this practical shares – it is not a Biowasm build.
Compiler: Emscripten 6.0.10. PCRE2: the 8-bit library, with Unicode support, without the
just-in-time compiler (there is none for WebAssembly: grep uses PCRE2's interpreter, as it does on
any computer where the just-in-time compiler is not available). grep: configured with
--enable-perl-regexp --disable-nls; no threads.
Everything needed to build it again is in ../../../licenses/:
  sources/grep-3.11.tar.xz              the source of the release, as published by GNU
  sources/pcre2-10.42.tar.bz2           the source of the release, as published by the PCRE2 project
  grep-perl-build/build-grep-perl.sh    the build script (it also records exit(status), sets the
                                        program's name and the name of its .wasm file in the loader)
  grep-perl-build/grep-perl-splice.c    a splice() that always fails with EINVAL (see below)
  grep-perl-build/README.txt            how to run it

Both sources are compiled unchanged. One function is added at link time: Emscripten's headers
declare splice() and SPLICE_F_MOVE, but its C library has no splice(). grep calls it only to skip
the rest of a pipe when its own output goes to /dev/null, and is written to read instead when the
call fails with EINVAL – which the added function always does.

Changes to the JavaScript loader, grep-perl.js (made by the build script): exit(status) is recorded
as Module.__exitStatus, so that the terminal of the practical keeps the exit status; the program is
called "grep" (its messages begin "grep:"), whatever name the runtime hands it; and the loader looks
for grep-perl.wasm.

In the terminal of the practical this program runs when a grep command asks for Perl patterns: -P
alone or in a group of letters (-oP, -oPm1), --perl-regexp. (The Biowasm build of grep 3.7 in
../3.7/, which runs every other grep, was built without PCRE.) So "grep -P --version" says 3.11,
and "grep --version" 3.7.

Checked against GNU grep 3.11 with PCRE2 10.42 on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04) with 874 command lines that an
independent reviewer wrote to find differences – what -o prints after \K, look-behind and look-ahead,
possessive counts and atomic groups, references to groups, classes and escapes, characters outside
ASCII, lines that end with a carriage return, files with NUL bytes, patterns that PCRE2 refuses,
the backtracking limit, lines of context, -m, -r, -f, -z. What "grep -P" printed and its exit status
were the same in all of them but one: "grep -P x f > f", where the terminal has emptied the file before
grep looks (status 1) and GNU grep refuses a file that is also its output (status 2).
